messages:
sarah_marketing: Quick thread — need a short, sharp battlecard iteration for next week's launch post and the webinar. Focus: how Redwood beats big cloud AI endpoints on predictable latency/cost. Two asks: 1) 1–2 hero bullets for the launch post; 2) routing play for SDRs when customers mention 'managed endpoint' vs 'self-host'.

alex_growth: Love it. For hero bullets: 'Consistent p99 latency across mixed workloads' and '40% unit-cost savings via batching + KV caching for common prompts' — both backed by infra numbers. want concise phrasing. :thumbsup:

maria_field: For SDR routing — if they say "managed endpoint" route to SALES_PRE-SALES with lead tag "ops-sensitive". If they say "self-host" route to PLATFORM_EVALS and include infra checklist. We should standardize the tag names.

tom_k: Can we add a short benchmark line: "Our in-house 8x sequence benchmark: equivalent throughput at 60% of cloud vendor cost in our internal test bed" — don't claim public numbers until legal signs off.

jordan_pm: Also recommend a quick objection handler: customer: 'we already have cloud endpoints' -> response: 'Great — Redwood can run as hosted or private; same API, predictable SLA and fallbacks to cheaper model variants when capacity spikes.' Keep it 1–2 lines.

maria_field: Also add routing nuance: Mid-market inbound flagged as 'compliance required' should bypass SDRs and go straight to enterprise AE queue with a note: "Private/VPC conversation likely".

alex_growth: For the launch post hero copy, how about: "Ship LLM features without surprising bills — consistent latency, smarter batching, and policies for graceful fallback." Short and producty.

sarah_marketing: Nice. Can someone draft two one-liners and a 3-bullet battlecard (competitor claim / our counter) by EOD? We'll use them for the post, webinar one-sheeter, and SDR slack snippets.

tom_k: I'll draft competitor-counter bullets. Example format:
- Competitor: 'managed endpoints scale easily' — Our counter: 'Yes — but at variable cost; Redwood Dedicated offers both predictability and autoscaling policies that limit spend surprises.'
- Competitor: 'we have the best latency' — Our counter: 'Redwood runtime picks kernels + batching that keep p99 low across models.'
- Competitor: 'self-host is cheaper' — Our counter: 'Not when you factor in SRE ops and KV cache engineering — Redwood Optimize reduces ops lift + unit cost.'

dev_rel_bot: deploy-bot: New benchmark artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-marketing/benchmarks/march-2026/8x-seq-report.pdf

alex_growth: Perfect, link that in the post. Also create two SDR snippets: one for cloud vendor comparisons, one for infra vendor conversations. Keep them <140 chars.

jordan_pm: For the webinar narrative, propose a 3-act structure: 1) The problem (unpredictable inference economics), 2) Demo (Redwood routing + fallback + console), 3) Proof (benchmarks + customer story). End with CTA: 'Request a dedicated cost run'.

maria_field: I'm worried about legal on benchmarking. tom, can you ping legal for a short review loop? We should have an approved safe phrasing: 'internal benchmark' vs 'public benchmark'.

tom_k: On it. I'll ping legal and put the draft behind a placeholder phrasing: "internal tests show" until cleared.

sarah_marketing: Action list: tom — competitor bullet drafts + legal ping (due today). alex — two SDR snippets + pull benchmark link into post (due today). jordan — webinar 3-act outline + slide titles (due tomorrow). maria — finalize routing tags and AE queue rules in Zendesk (due today). I'll assemble the battlecard one-pager after drafts land.

alex_growth: SDR snippets (first pass):
- Cloud snippet: "We offer predictable inference costs and p99 SLAs across hosted & private deployments — want a quick cost comparison?"
- Infra snippet: "Reduce ops lift: same API everywhere + dedicated capacity and caching for steady unit economics. Want a checklist?"

maria_field: Routing tag list (draft): [ops-sensitive, compliance-required, infra-eval, product-led]. I'll map them to queues in Zendesk and share a short doc.

sarah_marketing: Great. One more thing: webinar tease copy for social — 2 variants: aggressive econ angle & product demo angle. Alex, can you prep both?

alex_growth: Yep — aggressive econ: "How to avoid surprise LLM bills: benchmarks and playbooks." Product demo: "See a single API route to hosted, dedicated, and private inference."

tom_k: Legal replied: ok to say 'internal benchmarks show' and 'in our tests, we saw ~40% lower unit cost' but no vendor names or absolute claims. I'll incorporate.

sarah_marketing: Awesome. If all good, I'll pull together the battlecard doc and drop it in #marketing-assets tonight. Thanks everyone. :rocket:

maria_field: I'll update the Zendesk mapping and post the routing matrix in the thread when done.

alex_growth: Once battlecard is in assets, I'll create a short Notion checklist for the SDRs and tag the sales lead.

jordan_pm: I'll write the slide titles and a 1-slide demo script and drop in the assets doc tomorrow morning.

sarah_marketing: Closing note — try to keep language customer-facing and avoid internal jargon (e.g., no "KV cache" in SDR snippets; use "smart caching").
